newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S.Australia to sell timber processing plant.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S.Australia to sell timber processing plant.

text.p: The South Australian government said on Wednesday it had approved the sale of a decommissioned timber processing plant and equipment, but it expected to recoup only a fraction of its A$56 million investment.

Treasurer Stephen Baker said the sale of the plant's building and land at Mount Gambier, in the State's south-east, would follow the sale of the plant and equipment, in "the final chapter of yet another Labor Government debacle".

Baker said in a statement the South Australian Timber Corp (SATCO) and the former State Government Insurance Commission (SGIC) had been joint partners in the project to commercialise the 'scrimber' process invented by the Commonwealth Science and Industry Research Organisation (CSIRO).
Scrimber is a reconstituted structural timber product produced from young timber plantation thinnings.
"This is yet another example of a highly speculative venture with statutory authorities such as SATCO and SCIC should never have been involved in," he said.

The two bodies had invested around A$56 million, including interest foregone on the investment, before problems experienced in commissioning the plant led the former Labor government to withdraw from the project in 1991, he said.
Baker said in 1993 an agreement allowed U.S.-based Georgia Pacific Corp to develop the scrimber process at the site at its own cost.

"Although the company is still deciding whether to proceed with the building of its first manufacturing plant in the U.S., it has indicated it is not interested in purchasing the Mount Gambier plant," he said. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
